posts.text:
Say an AI writes you a poem. Fine, poems evaporate.

Now imagine one that files your taxes, cancels your flight, and actually refunds the miles.

Microsoft shipped Agent Framework skills yesterday. Basically a manual for your coding agent that says "here's how to not wire your tools backwards." That's a gift. Also, draw your own conclusions about what was happening before.

U Mobile in Malaysia seems to have cracked something real. Their AiDaH agents run 150+ operational scenarios on Bedrock AgentCore and cut some ticket categories by 84%. The machine checks configs, verifies eligibility, finds the break, proposes a fix. All before a human opens their eyes.

Here's what nobody puts in the press release: content is forgiving. Actions leave receipts. Every decision an agent makes is a liability with a timestamp, sitting in a log someone will read at 2am while a manager asks why the warehouse shut down.

The hard skill now is building agents you can explain to a regulator, debug when everything's on fire, and gracefully shut down when they get creative about what "refund" means. Everything else is just wiring.

#AgenticAI #EnterpriseReliability

record.text:
Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on November 9. Fable handles general work. Mythos stays gated behind verification programs for cybersecurity and life sciences research.

The pricing is concrete. Eight dollars per million input tokens, forty for output. Speed claims are concrete. Everything else in the announcement - formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem, solving open physics problems - is Anthropic's own testing. Your mileage will vary.

I keep noticing the data retention clause. Zero retention only if you qualify and request it, and only guaranteed through June 2027. Otherwise, thirty days with human safety review. Procurement reads the fine print before the compliance team asks why customer data is sitting in someone else's logs.

The cadence is the real story. Another model version, another regression cycle, another set of prompts to validate. The gap between benchmark brags and production reliability stays wide. Anthropic's tests run on curated tasks. Your agents run on real user input that misspells "refund," asks for refunds that don't match policy, and hopes you don't notice.

Prompt testing, structured outputs, and having a real plan for when the model goes off-script. Those are still your job. The new weights just change how fast the surprises arrive.

https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2

details: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are described as the same underlying model, with Fable having strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards for general availability, while Mythos is available via verification programs for advanced work in cybersecurity and life sciences. [A1, A2]
The new models are priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, which is lower than the previous version, and can generate outputs up to 30% faster. [A1, A3]

During pre-release testing, Anthropic states the models helped complete complex software migrations, design electronic devices, solve open physics problems, and formalize the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem. [A1, A4]

Claude Fable 5.2 on Amazon Bedrock requires data retention for up to 30 days with human safety review by default, but eligible customers can use it with zero data retention through at least June 30, 2027. [A2, A3]
